audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gave Mordekaiser 6 of 7 stages and Zac none, in a matchup Zac wins 52.45% over 204 games.
audit.why: A chart that never hands Zac a single stage cannot produce a winning record. The full layer's own phases[] for this matchup already read Mordekaiser, Skill, Zac, Zac, Mordekaiser, Zac, Zac — so the two layers were also contradicting each other. Mordekaiser genuinely owns levels 1-6; Zac's edge is the tank/peel scaling after items, which is where the win rate is earned.
audit.corrected: Mordekaiser 1-6, Skill at first item, Zac at 2+ items.

audit.whatIsWrong: Realm of Death was treated as an ever-present threat with no number attached.
audit.why: Realm of Death is 140/120/100s. At rank 1 that is a 140-second window in which Mordekaiser has no way to isolate anyone. That is the single largest punish window in the lane and it was never stated, so the player has no reason to step up after he uses it.
audit.corrected: Realm is 140s at rank 1 — once spent, the next two minutes of side lane are yours.

audit.whatIsWrong: No concrete cooldown to trade around for the pre-6 lane.
audit.why: Obliterate is 8/7/6/5/4s and is his main chunk. An 8-second gap at rank 1 is a real trading window for a champion whose own W is on a flat 5s.
audit.corrected: Trade in the 8s after Obliterate whiffs.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never mentioned Grievous Wounds even though Indestructible is the reason Zac loses extended trades.
audit.why: Indestructible stores damage dealt and taken into a shield that he can consume to heal, on 12/11/10/9/8s. Against a grind champion like Zac that heal is the whole matchup, and _missing-interactions.json flags exactly this (rule needs-antiheal). The full layer's itemization line already says anti-heal; the content layer, which is what the player actually reads in lane, did not.
audit.corrected: Build MR plus Grievous Wounds; MR alone loses to the W heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late-game section concluded the matchup "becomes a skill matchup", which understates a 52.45% result and contradicts the win-rate data it sits next to.
audit.why: Zac's win condition here is not parity — it is that a full-tank Zac converts the lane deficit into peel value that Mordekaiser's single-target ultimate cannot answer.
audit.corrected: Late tips to Zac; the record is banked in teamfights, not in lane.

Realm is 140s at rank 1 though — the moment he spends it, the next two minutes of side lane are yours.

He'll still win the raw 1v1, so don't duel him; play the teamfight and this becomes a skill matchup around who lands their ult on the right target.
edits.after: The lane tips your way with items — as a full tank you soak his magic DPS and, crucially, your job shifts to peel: use E-flash and R (Let's Bounce!) to lock Morde off your carries and body-block his Realm target. He'll still win the raw 1v1, so don't duel him; play the teamfight, because that is where the 52% is actually banked.

edits.after: - Mordekaiser Realm of Death (140s at rank 1): matchup-defining — his 1v1 realm, and two free minutes once spent. - Obliterate (8s): his chunk. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

SEPARATE SYSTEMIC ISSUE the user should know about: content win[] and full phases[].side disagree for this matchup and for six of the other eight in my slice. The full layer's phases[].side look template-generated (Skill,Zac,Zac,Skill,Skill,Zac,Zac or an enemy-heavy variant) rather than authored per matchup. I could not repair phases[].side through the applier because apply-proposals.js requires a full-layer `before` of at least 12 characters and those values are 3-11 chars ('Zac', 'Skill', 'Ornn'), so every such edit is rejected as non-distinctive. Same limitation blocks fixing diff/tone/diffRating. These need a separate pass or a targeted script. Also flagged and NOT edited: _missing-interactions.json claims 'Your Obliterate (Q) shuts off Zac's Elastic Slingshot (E)' — that is derived from a bogus grounding flag on Obliterate ('smashes the ground' matched the keyword). Mordekaiser has no grounding. Do not let that headline reach the data.
